explained.tdh.design.meta.title: Consolidation design · 6529 Explained
explained.tdh.design.meta.description: Why every pair of wallets must link both ways, what that protects, and what it does not.
explained.tdh.design.title: Why every pair of wallets links both ways
explained.tdh.design.lede: Asking every pair to link both ways costs a few transactions, and of the rules tested, it is the only one where no smaller group of your wallets can add an outside wallet.
explained.tdh.design.rule.label: The rule
explained.tdh.design.rule.title: Registrations, pair by pair
explained.tdh.design.rule.body: Each pair of wallets registers a consolidation in both directions in 6529's delegation contract, where consolidation is use case {useCase}, on Any Collection or The Memes. Two wallets need {two} registrations, three need {three}, and four need {four}. Registrations do not expire: a link lasts until one of its wallets revokes it.
explained.tdh.design.order.label: Signing order
explained.tdh.design.order.question: A, B and C are linked. D joins. Does any snapshot see a split?
explained.tdh.design.protects.label: What it protects
explained.tdh.design.protects.outside: No smaller group of your wallets can add an outside wallet: a wallet joins only if linked with every member.
explained.tdh.design.protects.old: Old registrations cannot fill the fourth slot: links from before {date} never form a group of four.
explained.tdh.design.protects.keys: Make any one wallet safer. Each linked wallet is a full key to your profile; four wallets are four keys.
explained.tdh.design.protects.manager: Protect against one delegation manager acting for all your wallets: its key alone can change your consolidation.
explained.tdh.design.protects.tested: Each candidate rule was checked exhaustively for a group of up to four wallets. That covers every set of registrations an attacker holding one to three of your wallets could sign, and every order in which a new wallet's transactions can land. The cheapest alternative saved two transactions, once. P26's rule was checked against 6529.io's own code on {graphs} random link graphs and the real rows. These are 6529's own tests, not an outside audit.
explained.tdh.design.hwk.analysisBody: The earlier TDH pages' Consolidation design ({frontend}), How it was tested: each candidate rule against every set of registrations an attacker holding some of your wallets could sign, and the grouping code it pins ({backend}).
